reason: E1 and E2 show that CoCrNiMn filler powder forms Fex(CoCrNiMn)Tiy HEAs and reduces Fe-Ti IMCs in TA1/Q345 bimetallic sheet welding, with tensile strength reaching ~293 MPa. However, the cited evidence is limited to a specific Ti/steel bimetallic sheet at room temperature; no evidence supports application to a generic damaged component, aggressive high-temperature/stress conditions, or improved toughness and hot-cracking resistance. E3 is about oxide ceramics and thin-film HEAs, providing no direct support for the welding or mechanical property claims.
premises: Laser welding with CoCrNiMn filler powder can in-situ form Fex(CoCrNiMn)Tiy HEAs in the weld metal
In-situ HEA formation reduces brittle Fe-Ti intermetallic compounds at the welding interface
Reducing Fe-Ti IMCs improves mechanical properties (strength, toughness, hot-cracking resistance) compared to traditional fusion welding
The approach is applicable to damaged high-value components under aggressive high-temperature, high-stress conditions
